title.narrative: Support to the purchase of Caritas Port-au-Prince office and equipment

description.narrative:
On January 12th 2010, Haiti was rocked by its strongest earthquake in more than 200 years, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale. The earthquake struck the West, Southwest and Nippes department with the epicentre some 17 kms southwest of Haiti’s capitale, Port-au-Prince. The Port-au-Prince metropolitan area (including the towns of Port-au-Prince, Carrefour, Pétionville, Delmas, Tabarre, Cité-Soleil and Kenscoff) suffered a substantial amount of damage.
The destruction of infrastructure is colossal. About 105,000 homes were totally destroyed and over 208,000 were damaged. More than 1,300 educational institutions and more than 50 hospitals and health centres have collapsed or are unusable. The Presidential Palace, Parliament, law courts, and most ministerial and public administration buildings have been destroyed.
The Caritas Port-au-Prince office, located near the national Palace, was totally destroyed together with the archbishop house and the historical cathedral of Port-au-Prince. Since the catastrophe, the office of Caritas Port-au-Prince was located in two rooms made available by Caritas Haiti.
This grant is a contribution to Caritas Port-au-Prince for the purchase of a new office in order to improve their capacity to respond to the emergency and recovery operation in Haiti.
